text:
maria: Hey infra — hitting repeated VolumeThroughputExceeded on ML checkpoint restores in ap-southeast-1 during our nightly shard restores. Seeing snapshot restore speeds ~20-30 MB/s per volume, but we need ~200 MB/s. Could we request an account-level EBS throughput/IOPS increase and snapshot concurrency bump? We're spinning up p4de.24xlarge restores across a 20-node cluster for model retraining.

kevin: Can you paste a recent error log and the instance type? Also which account/region? @maria

maria: region: ap-southeast-1, account: 123456789012, instance: p4de.24xlarge, command: `aws ec2 create-volume --snapshot-id snap-0abcd --volume-type gp3 --size 4000 --throughput 1000` — errors: `VolumeThroughputExceeded`, `SnapshotCopyThrottled`. Happened around 03:10 UTC last night. :grimacing:

raj: Sounds like both per-volume throughput and snapshot API concurrent copy quotas. AWS quotas to request: "EBS Snapshot API requests (per region per account)", "EBS IOPS per account" and possibly "EBS throughput". Also check S3 transfer quotas if cross-region snapshot copy uses S3.

kevin: We'll need approximate RPS and bytes/s: roughly 20 volumes being restored concurrently, each needs ~200 MB/s for the training shuffle => ~4 GB/s total. Snapshot copy requests are roughly 10-15 parallel copy ops during restore phase.

sam: FYI this is triggering ticket 987654321 with aws; they asked for metrics. Can someone share CloudWatch graphs for `VolumeReadBytes` and `SnapshotCopyBytes` for last 24h? I'll attach.

maria: attaching graphs (omitted in thread). Also seeing a bucket of snapshot copy errors: `ExceededProvisionedThroughput`.

ops-bot: Created internal ticket INF-2026-0834 to track this. Assigned to @kevin and @raj. ETA for AWS escalation 48-72h. :spiral_calendar:

alice: Could we try a short-term workaround: stagger restores, reduce per-volume throughput settings (down to 100MB/s) and use block-level parallelism across fewer nodes? Might reduce cluster throughput but keep training running.

maria: We tried staggering but job deadline is tight. Requesting two things: 1) increase account-level snapshot copy concurrency to 50 (currently 20) in ap-southeast-1; 2) increase account-level EBS aggregate throughput quota to 8000 MB/s or equivalent IOPS to support 20x 4000GB gp3 volumes at higher throughput. Also request guidance if we should move to io2 or provisioned-io2?

raj: For the immediate quota request I'll raise with AWS support: quota code EBS-IOPS-ACCOUNT-AGG and SNAPSHOT-COPY-CONC. I'll propose the numbers you suggested. For longer term, consider distributed checkpointing using S3 or using instance-local NVMe ephemeral for warm caches. Also quantify cost if we move to io2.

kevin: Opening AWS support case now — Case #SR-1122334455 created. Escalation requested. Please add any billing justification (we'll include "training runs for production models with committed reserved capacity").

maria: Thanks. Can you CC the accounts team for cost approval? @alice

alice: On it. Approving for emergency uplift for 72 hours while we wait for permanent quotas.

sam: AWS responded: asking for peak sustained bytes/s and peak snapshot API calls per minute. We replied with the graphs. They flagged possible need for region capacity planning for ap-southeast-1 for gp3 throughput.

ops-bot: AWS case SR-1122334455 updated: "Quota increased provisionally to 6,000 MB/s aggregate for account in ap-southeast-1 pending verification. Snapshot concurrency increased to 40. Monitoring for 72 hours." Ticket link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=SR-1122334455

maria: Verified restores now at ~150 MB/s per volume, cluster got enough throughput to continue. Running training now. Will monitor and post post-mortem.

raj: After we stabilize let's plan a design doc for checkpointing strategy and cost tradeoffs. Assigning to myself and @maria.

maria: Thanks everyone. Closing action: INF-2026-0834 -> will update with postmortem in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
